name: Sentinel A4 air defense radar (AN/MPQ-64A4)
description: X-band digital AESA (GaN), 360 deg with stop-and-stare, -15 deg to zenith. Army SHORAD acquisition radar against FW/RW/CM/RAM and UAS. No public small-UAS detection range; ring is a role planning factor.

sectorDeg.source: Lockheed Martin Sentinel A4 product card (2024)

elevationDeg.source: Lockheed Martin Sentinel A4 product card (2024)

rangeAccuracyM.note: Class median of the sourced target-acquisition radars: lib-rps42 50; median 50 m.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced target-acquisition radars: lib-rps42 0.5; median 0.5 deg.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced target-acquisition radars: lib-rps42 0.5; median 0.5 deg.

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 360° radar is recorded at 1. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: Lockheed Martin publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. Sentinel rotates at 30 rpm with electronic back-scan (legacy A3 sheet), which holds the pencil beam on a target beyond the mechanical 2° / 180°/s = 11 ms, so the e-scan literature dwell is used.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: Lockheed Martin publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. Sentinel rotates at 30 rpm with electronic back-scan (legacy A3 sheet), which holds the pencil beam on a target beyond the mechanical 2° / 180°/s = 11 ms, so the e-scan literature dwell is used.
